predecessors.name: Seleucid Empire
predecessors.text: the Seleucid satrapy of the Erythraean Sea and Antiochia in Susiana, which Antiochus IV gave Hyspaosines to govern in 166/5 BC

successors.name: Sasanian Empire
successors.text: Characene taken by Ardashir I: 'he invaded Characene State in the mouth of Tigris and took it' (Ardashir I page)

capitals.name: Charax Spasinu (Alexandria, Antiochia, Jebel Khayabir near Naysan)

ledger.x: 141 BC: Hyspaosines declares independence at the head of the Persian Gulf.
127 BC: Hyspaosines seizes Babylon from the Parthians.
November 127 BC: the Parthian general Timarchus retakes Babylon, 'at the start of November 127 BC'.
124 BC: Hyspaosines accepts Parthian suzerainty and keeps ruling Characene as a vassal.
116: Trajan sails down the Tigris to the Persian Gulf and 'received the submission of Athambelus, the ruler of Charax', a brief Roman client status for Characene.
117: the Roman client status lapses with Trajan's withdrawal and death.
221/222: the vassalage ends with the kingdom when Ardashir I conquers Characene.
221/222: Ardashir I conquers Characene and the kingdom ends.

wars.name: Hyspaosines' invasion of Babylonia
wars.outcome: Hyspaosines held Babylon for part of 127 BC; Timarchus retook it at the start of November 127; in 124 BC Hyspaosines was forced to acknowledge Parthian suzerainty and died on 11 June 124.

wars.name: Trajan's Parthian campaign (Characene)
wars.outcome: Trajan reached Characene, where Attambelos VII ruled as a friend of Rome; Trajan withdrew in 117 (Parthian Empire page); the pages record no change of border.

wars.name: Ardashir I's conquest of Characene
wars.outcome: Ardashir defeated the Characene forces and, in the later Arab histories, killed the last ruler; the capital became Astarabad-Ardashir.

certainty.note: No boundary on any page; the Tigris-Karkheh delta and the Gulf coast are approximate.
